title: Fix JSON parse errors on DELETE 204 with parseResponseSafely

helper_function.name: parseResponseSafely
helper_function.purpose: Safely parse HTTP responses with proper content-type checking and fallback handling
features: Returns null for 204/205 No Content (no parse attempt)
Checks content-type header before parsing JSON
Falls back to { rawText } for non-JSON responses
Handles malformed JSON gracefully with try-catch
Prevents console errors from parse failures

changes: Replaced unconditional 'await res.json()' with fetch + parseResponseSafely
Extract error messages from parsed response (message, error, or rawText)
Handle 404 responses gracefully (return false, clean up local state)
Proper error message construction for non-ok responses
Maintain optimistic UI updates and background refresh

improvements: Differentiate between success (true) and not-found (false) from deleteAttribute
Show appropriate toast for both cases (deleted vs. already deleted)
Enhanced error message extraction from Error objects and structured responses
Log rawText responses to console for debugging HTML error pages
Ensure finally block always resets UI state (selection, form, saving, refresh)

coverage: Empty body with no content-type → null
Non-empty body with no content-type → { rawText }

technical_notes.why_204_causes_error: HTTP 204 No Content has no response body. Calling res.json() on it attempts to parse an empty string as JSON, which throws a SyntaxError. The old fetchJSON helper prevented this by reading res.text() first, but deleteAttribute was calling res.json() directly.
technical_notes.why_parseResponseSafely_is_better: It's a single helper that handles all edge cases: 204/205, content-type checking, malformed JSON, HTML error pages. Can be reused across all HTTP operations.
technical_notes.content_type_header_importance: Many proxies/servers return HTML error pages (404, 500) with text/html content-type. Attempting JSON.parse on HTML causes cryptic errors. parseResponseSafely checks content-type first.
technical_notes.fallback_to_rawText: When server returns non-JSON (HTML, plain text), we preserve it as { rawText } for debugging. The UI can log it to console and show a friendly generic message to the user.
technical_notes.ui_finally_block: The finally block in handleDelete ensures UI state (selection, form, saving) always resets, regardless of success/failure. This prevents stuck UI states.
